Claude's conclusion:
### Root cause

Live inspection of the paused device shows this is a **startup/convergence race during NI activation**, not a persistent misconfiguration. At the moment of failure, `/run/zedrouter/NetworkInstanceStatus/3a39f4fe-....json` showed the NI's `Ports` list still using raw kernel-assigned interface names (`eth0`/`eth1`/`eth2`/`eth3`), while `PortProber` had only just started probing them (`"PortProber: Started port probing for route dst=0.0.0.0/0 ..."` at `07:03:55.745786`), producing the `"... is not matching any port"` error within the same millisecond — before any probe result could possibly have arrived. The device log confirms the actual fix-up happens ~49s later: at `07:04:44` zedrouter removes the probed ports named `eth0..eth3` and re-adds them as `ethernet0..ethernet3` (the proper logical adapter names), after which `PortProber` immediately resolves both the `internet` and `httpserver` labeled routes to `ethernet0`. So the NI is activated and its static-route labels are evaluated against transient/temporary port names before the device's final logical port naming has been applied, and the test's `niHasError` `StopIf` treats this transient `ZNETINST_STATE_ERROR` as fatal rather than waiting it out (consistent with 19.5s elapsed vs. the test's `StopIf`/early-bail behavior).

`TestPropagatedRoutes`, which ran immediately before in this suite, passed cleanly, so there's no shared cause with another failure in this run.

This is a known, recurring issue per the ledger: the identical failure signature (same `eth0/eth1/eth2/eth3` naming, same `networkErr` text for `internet`/`httpserver` labels "is not matching any port", same `niHasError` quick-bail) appeared in the **2026-11-22** entry (2.116s failure), which was diagnosed there as a startup convergence race with transient bogus routes. A second, differently-shaped manifestation of the same test (slow TCP-probe convergence past the 10-minute budget) also recurred on 2026-11-23. So `TestLocalNIWithMultiplePorts` in `TestAppRoutingSuite` has been intermittently failing on NI-activation convergence races since at least 2026-11-22, and tonight's failure adds concrete evidence (the `eth0→ethernet0` rename event) pinpointing one specific cause of that race: route-label resolution running against pre-rename port names.

networkID:"d8b70e83-e58f-4744-8256-c9e36d5f9269"  networkVersion:"1"  instType:2  displayname:"ni-eth0"  bridgeNum:4  bridgeIPAddr:"10.50.0.1"  ipAssignments:{macAddress:"00:16:3e:06:00:04"  ipAddress:"10.50.0.1"}  networkErr:{description:"failed to select ports for network instance d8b70e83-e58f-4744-8256-c9e36d5f9269: no port is matching label 'ethernet0'"  timestamp:{seconds:1795504735  nanos:955882760}  severity:SEVERITY_ERROR}  state:ZNETINST_STATE_ERROR  mtu:1500

Claude's conclusion:
### Root cause

Live logs show zedrouter failed sanity-checking `ni-eth0` (port label `ethernet0`) at `07:18:55.955` with `"no port is matching label 'ethernet0'"`, right as `nim` was mid-flight switching the device's active DevicePortConfig from the generic "lastresort" DPC (ports named plain `eth0`/`eth1`) to the final controller-supplied "zedagent" DPC (ports relabeled `ethernet0`/`ethernet1`). The nim log at `07:18:54.486-07:18:54.5xx` shows it tearing down the DHCP clients/routes for `eth0`/`eth1` and reconfiguring under the new logical labels in the same window the NI (created at `07:18:54.527`) was being activated — so `DeviceNetworkStatus` momentarily had no port matching the label `ethernet0` when zedrouter went to select ports, exactly the kind of transient convergence gap seen before. `PortProber` only picked up `ethernet0` at `07:19:26.480`, long after the test's 26.6s `StopIf` budget had already given up.

This is the same underlying race already diagnosed for `TestLocalNIWithMultiplePorts` earlier in this very run (`live-investigation.md`): NI activation and route/port-label resolution racing ahead of the device's DPC/logical-port-naming convergence, just manifesting here as a port-selection failure instead of a route-matching failure. It is **not** a new, independent bug in this run.

Per the ledger, this exact `TestApplicationGateway` failure signature (`"no port is matching label"`) hasn't appeared before, but the broader class of issue — NI activation racing ahead of device port/DPC convergence — has been a known recurring problem in `TestAppRoutingSuite` since at least 2026-11-22 (affecting `TestLocalNIWithMultiplePorts` on 2026-11-22 and 2026-11-23, and now this run).

Claude's conclusion:
### Root cause

Live inspection of the paused device confirms the NI's two label-routed static routes diverged after `eth0` was set `AdminUp=false`: the "internet" route (gateway-ping probe) failed over to `ethernet3` almost instantly, but `/run/zedrouter/NetworkInstanceStatus/*.json` and `ip route show table 801` both show the "httpserver" route (TCP probe to `10.88.88.70:80`) still pinned to the dead `ethernet0` at the moment of timeout. The zedrouter log pinpoints why: `PortProber` didn't flip the httpserver route to `ethernet2` until `05:08:56` (`"Changing port from ethernet0 to ethernet2 ... (UP count = 1)"`), which is **11m33s** after Phase 2 began at `04:57:23` — 1m33s past the test's 10-minute `failoverTimeout`. This isn't a race; it's arithmetic baked into `PortProber`'s `DefaultConfig()` (`pkg/pillar/portprober/portprober.go`): user-defined (TCP) probes run at `NHProbeInterval * NHToUserProbeRatio` = 15s × 10 = 150s, and require `MaxContFailCnt`+1 = 5 consecutive failures before declaring DOWN, i.e. a deterministic ~12.5-minute detection floor that the test's 10-minute budget can't accommodate — unlike the gateway-ping route, which gets fast "sudden change" detection. This is a different failure mode than the other failure in tonight's run (`TestDNSFunctionality`'s DNS-not-available race) and than 2026-11-21's root cause (NI startup convergence/`niHasError` false-positive), so no shared cause there. However, 2026-11-22's ledger entry for this same test explicitly cites "PortProber logs" as giving "a conclusive timeline for the root cause," strongly suggesting the identical slow-TCP-probe-convergence issue was already found the prior night — so this looks like a recurring, deterministically-reproducible issue since at least 2026-11-22, likely needing either a longer `failoverTimeout` in the test or a faster detection path for user-probe-based NI routes.

networkID:"e885d244-90d9-4cc1-8e71-c71bfeff1674"  networkVersion:"1"  instType:2  displayname:"multi-port-ni"  activated:true  CurrentUplinkIntf:"eth0"  ports:"eth0"  ports:"eth1"  ports:"eth2"  ports:"eth3"  bridgeNum:1  bridgeName:"bn1"  bridgeIPAddr:"10.50.0.1"  ipAssignments:{macAddress:"00:16:3e:06:00:01"  ipAddress:"10.50.0.1"}  networkErr:{description:"IP Route: {dst=0.0.0.0/0, gw=<nil>, port=internet, probe={enabledGwPing=true, gwPingMaxCost=5, userProbe=<none>}, preferLowerCost=true, preferStrongerWwanSignal=false} is not matching any port\nIP Route: {dst=10.88.88.0/24, gw=<nil>, port=httpserver, probe={enabledGwPing=true, gwPingMaxCost=0, userProbe=tcp://10.88.88.70:80}, preferLowerCost=true, preferStrongerWwanSignal=false} is not matching any port"  timestamp:{seconds:1795236601  nanos:313267473}  severity:SEVERITY_ERROR}  state:ZNETINST_STATE_ERROR  mtu:1500  ip_routes:{destination_network:"0.0.0.0/0"  gateway:"192.168.30.1"  port:"eth2"}  ip_routes:{destination_network:"0.0.0.0/0"  gateway:"172.22.10.1"  port:"eth0"}  ip_routes:{destination_network:"172.22.10.0/24"  port:"eth0"}  ip_routes:{destination_network:"192.168.30.0/24"  port:"eth2"}

Claude's conclusion:
### Root cause analysis

Live inspection shows the NI genuinely recovered on its own: the current `/run/zedrouter/NetworkInstanceStatus/e885d244-....json` on the device (modified at 04:52:15, ~2m13s after the failure at 04:50:02) now shows `"Error":""`, both static routes resolved to `SelectedPort:"ethernet0"`, and all four port subnets present in `CurrentRoutes` — exactly what the test is waiting for. The device's logs pinpoint why it took that long: at 04:51:51 zedrouter was still logging `IP Route: {... port=internet ...} is not matching any port` and `{... port=httpserver ...} is not matching any port`, and the `NetworkInstanceStatus` diff at that moment shows the kernel/zedrouter route state was still churning — `CurrentRoutes` transiently contained *three* simultaneous `0.0.0.0/0` entries (via `ethernet3`, `ethernet2`, and `ethernet1`), including bogus default routes on ports (eth1, eth2) that by design (per the test's own topology comment) should never have outside/default reachability. This is a startup convergence race: four differently-configured ports (two DHCP, two static) were brought up together with a brand-new NI, and until the route/port state settled (~2 minutes), the shared-label route resolver saw an inconsistent/incomplete picture and flagged the NI as `ERROR`. The test's `niHasError` `StopIf` callback (evetest/tests/networking/helpers_test.go:33) treats the very first sighting of `ZNETINST_STATE_ERROR` as fatal, so `Eventually` bailed after only 2.1s instead of tolerating this transient convergence window — `TestPropagatedRoutes`, which ran immediately before in this same suite run, passed cleanly, so this isn't shared with an earlier failure in the run. This specific test doesn't appear in `live-ledger.md` (which only has one prior night, 2026-11-20, and doesn't mention `TestLocalNIWithMultiplePorts` or `TestAppRoutingSuite`), so it's not a confirmed recurring/known issue yet, though it echoes the same general theme as that night's `TestMgmtTrafficRoutedViaApp` failure (slow convergence of network-port state after a config change outrunning the test's wait/fail logic).
